name: Customer Onboarding Checklist
description: A checklist for guiding new product or SaaS customers from account setup to activation and first value.

items.text: Confirm the signup and verify the customer's email address.
Provision the account with the correct plan, limits and permissions.
Guide the user through profile and workspace basics on first login.
Help connect essential integrations or import existing data.
items.note: Imported data makes the product feel useful immediately.

items.text: Confirm login works across the devices the customer will actually use.
Send a warm welcome message that sets expectations for the journey.
Share a short getting-started guide or quick-start video.
Point the user to support channels, help center and community.
Set a clear first goal so the user knows what success looks like.
Offer a personalized walkthrough or onboarding call for higher-tier plans.
Guide the user to complete the core action that delivers value.
Remove friction from the activation flow with inline tips or tooltips.
Celebrate the first value moment so the user notices the benefit.
items.note: Name the win in-product — 'You just shipped your first report.'

items.text: Suggest a logical next step that deepens product usage.
Track activation milestones so you know who has and hasn't reached value.
Share role-relevant tutorials rather than the entire feature list.
Deliver tips progressively as the user is ready for each feature.
Invite the user to a live webinar or office hours if available.
Provide templates or examples that speed up real work.
Confirm the user can complete their key tasks without help.
Set up helpful notifications or reminders without overwhelming the user.
Encourage the user to invite teammates or expand usage where relevant.
Highlight an underused feature that matches the customer's goal.
Monitor usage signals to spot drop-off before it becomes churn.
items.note: A sudden activity drop is an early churn warning.

items.text: Re-engage inactive users with a targeted, value-focused message.
Run an early check-in to confirm the customer is getting value.
Collect feedback with a short survey or quick onboarding rating.
Resolve any blockers surfaced during the check-in promptly.
Share a clear path to upgrade or expand once value is proven.
Hand off long-term accounts to ongoing success with full context.
items.note: Document goals and milestones so success picks up seamlessly.

faq.q: What is a customer onboarding checklist?
faq.a: It is a step-by-step list that guides a new product or SaaS user from account setup through their first meaningful result, covering welcome, activation, training, first value and an early check-in.

faq.q: How is customer onboarding different from client onboarding?
faq.a: Customer onboarding gets an individual user successful with a product, often at scale and partly in-app. Client onboarding sets up a B2B service engagement with contracts, kickoff meetings and a project plan.

faq.q: What is the first value moment in onboarding?
faq.a: It is the point where a user experiences the core benefit they signed up for — their first completed task, report or saved time. Reaching it quickly is the strongest signal a customer will stay.

faq.q: Can I print this checklist or save it as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. The checklist prints cleanly on one page and downloads as a PDF, so product and success teams can keep a shared reference or attach it to an onboarding playbook.

faq.q: How do I adapt this checklist for my SaaS product?
faq.a: Replace the generic activation steps with the specific actions that lead to value in your product, set realistic timeframes for each milestone, then save your version as a PDF for the team.
